2.text: This is probably true, though their position does not quite correspond to the

3.text: usual position of the labret. These marks are now intended only as charms

4.text: against spirits. The same is true of other marks, representing human figures,

5.text: of which I shall speak later. I heard from the Kolyma Chukchee that in

6.text: ancient times a man, after killing an enemy, tattooed a dot on the back of

7.text: his right wrist. For each similar performance a dot was added, sometimes in

8.text: this way forming quite a line of dots running from the wrist toward the elbow.

12.text: PERSONAL ADORNMENT. — Chukchee men and women, embellish their per-

13.text: sons with various adornments of rudest fashion, most of which are regarded

14.text: as protecting charms or amulets. Most prominent among these are necklaces.

15.text: The ordinary type is a slender leather band (Fig. 187, a), much soiled, often

16.text: broken in one or two places and retied with ungainly

17.text: knots (see Fig. 190, a). In front is fastened a tiny pouch

18.text: for the tobacco-quid. An amulet sewed up in a piece of

19.text: leather may be added, or even a small figure carved of ivory

20.text: (Fig. 187, b). At present, however, beads are considered

21.text: best suited for this purpose. Some of those who have

22.text: been baptized add a brass crucifix.
